les: Die Kasteel: een gebou, baie stories
kaps_punt: Erfenis en veranderende identiteite: Voorbeeld: Die Kasteel: Wes-Kaap

items.bewering: Die Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie (VOC) was 'n Nederlandse handelsmaatskappy wat die Kaap beheer het.
items.bron: sahistory.org.za, 'Dutch settlement' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/article/dutch-settlement) and Stellenbosch ESAT entry on the VOC (https://esat.sun.ac.za/index.php/VOC): the Dutch East India Company, a Dutch trading company, set up the Cape station in 1652 and ruled the Cape until the British occupation of 1795. Full name 'Verenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie' matches the Afrikaans rendering.

items.bewering: Tussen 1666 en 1679 het die VOC die Kasteel die Goeie Hoop in Kaapstad in die Wes-Kaap gebou.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Castle of Good Hope (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_of_Good_Hope): built by the Dutch East India Company between 1666 and 1679, first stone laid 2 January 1666; Afrikaans name given there as 'Kasteel die Goeie Hoop'. sahistory.org.za, Dutch and British coastal fortifications 1665-1829 (https://sahistory.org.za/place/dutch-and-british-coastal-fortifications-cape-good-hope-1665-1829): foundation stone 1666. Cape Town Tourism (https://www.capetown.travel/fun-facts-about-the-castle-of-good-hope/) agrees on 1666-1679.

items.bewering: Die Kasteel was 'n vesting met dik klipmure.
items.bron: Castle of Good Hope official site, 'Between Stone and Silence: Rewriting the Castle of Good Hope' (https://www.castleofgoodhope.co.za/PDFs/Re-writing%20History.pdf): 'Behind its thick stone walls'. Wikipedia: a pentagonal stone bastion fort replacing the earlier clay-and-timber fort; sahistory.org.za: built in blue-stone.

items.bewering: Slawe, matrose en soldate het dit gebou.
items.bron: Camissa Museum, located inside the Castle (https://camissamuseum.co.za/): the Castle 'was built using the exploited labour of the enslaved'. Wikipedia: partially built by slave labour. Creamer Media, 'Major milestone for Castle of Good Hope' (2016): main building workforce about 300 sailors and soldiers from passing VOC ships, with slaves collecting and carrying the building material. gov.za, Minister Mapisa-Nqakula's speech at the Castle's 350 years, 9 Dec 2016 (https://www.gov.za/speeches/castle-good-hope-09-december-9-dec-2016-0000): builders worked 'side by side with Khoi-Khoi, African and Eastern slave labourers'. Sources differ on how much of the bricklaying itself slaves did, but all three groups named in the lesson are attested as the labour force; the lesson's list is not exhaustive (Khoikhoi workers also took part at times) and does not claim to be.

items.bewering: Die Kasteel was 'n teken van koloniale mag oor die Kaap en sy mense.
items.bron: gov.za speech, 9 Dec 2016: the Castle symbolises the start of an era that 'set our country on the destructive path of colonial injustice'. Castle of Good Hope official article 'Between Stone and Silence': efforts 'to transform the Castle from a symbol of colonial authority into a space of shared reflection'.

items.bewering: Vir die slawe het die Kasteel harde werk beteken wat hulle nie kon weier nie.
items.bron: Camissa Museum: 'built using the exploited labour of the enslaved'; Creamer Media (2016): slaves collected and conveyed all the building material; Wikipedia: partially built by slave labour. Forced, unpaid labour is what enslavement meant.

items.bewering: Vir die Khoi en die San het die mure gewys dat die VOC nou hul grond beheer.
items.bron: gov.za speech, 9 Dec 2016: 'the indigenous habitants of the Cape peninsula - the Khoi-Khoi and San' 'fought to retain their land and freedom'. Reporting on the Castle's 350th commemoration (IOL / Cape Times, 2016): to the indigenous people it became a symbol of dispossession of land and livestock, and a Khoisan commemoration member called it a physical symbol of their displacement. This is an interpretive claim and is stated as such by the Castle's own commemoration and by government.

items.bewering: Een gebou het dus vir verskillende mense iets anders beteken.
items.bron: Castle of Good Hope official article 'Between Stone and Silence': the Castle presents 'multiple, sometimes competing interpretations'; visitors' reactions differ by background. Follows from the three preceding verified claims.

items.bewering: Die Kasteel se mure staan nog.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Castle of Good Hope: the oldest existing building in South Africa; restored in the 1980s and the best-preserved VOC fort. Castle official site describes visitors moving through the yard and walls today.

items.bewering: Vandag is dit 'n erfenisterrein met museums.
items.bron: Castle of Good Hope official site (https://www.castleofgoodhope.co.za/): declared a historical monument in 1936, now a provincial heritage site. Wikipedia: houses the Castle Military Museum, the Cape Heritage Museum and the Iziko William Fehr Collection; Camissa Museum site states it is located within the Castle.

items.bewering: Lank het die museums veral die VOC se storie vertel.
items.bron: Castle of Good Hope official article 'Between Stone and Silence': museum staff describe 'a deliberate shift away from a singular colonial narrative', reframing 'what was once a largely celebratory account of Dutch rule'; earlier scholarship 'often focused on military and political narratives'. 'VOC se storie' is a fair Grade 5 rendering of 'a celebratory account of Dutch rule'.

items.bewering: Nou vertel hulle ook die stories van slawe en van Khoi- en San-gemeenskappe.
items.bron: Iziko, 'Rethinking the William Fehr Collection' (https://www.iziko.org.za/exhibitions/rethinking-the-william-fehr-collection/): reinterpretation discusses the labour of enslaved people and the resistance of Khoekhoe herders and San hunter-gatherers. Camissa Museum inside the Castle covers 'Cape Indigenous Africans' and 'African & Asian Enslaved Peoples'. Castle official article: exhibition rooms now 'juxtapose military artefacts with narratives of displacement and survival'. The same article records activists saying these stories remain underrepresented; the lesson's 'ook' claims inclusion, not equal weight, so it stays true.

items.bewering: 'n Museum is een manier waarop mense die verlede onthou en herdenk.
items.bron: Castle of Good Hope official article: the Castle 'operates both as a museum and a site of memory'. ICOM museum definition (2022): museums research, collect, conserve, interpret and exhibit heritage and offer experiences for reflection and knowledge sharing.

items.bewering: Namate Suid-Afrikaners hul eie geskiedenis vollediger begin vertel het, het die Kasteel se betekenis verander.
items.bron: Castle official article: 'interpretations of the Castle have changed significantly over time', newer research incorporating precolonial histories and oral traditions 'that were previously excluded'. gov.za speech 2016: call to 'transform the Castle from what it used to stand for then to a place of nation-building' through 'a balanced interpretation of history'.

items.bewering: Nasate van slawe en van die Khoi en San vind nou ook hul eie mense se storie daar.
items.bron: Camissa Museum (https://camissamuseum.co.za/), inside the Castle, tells 'the stories of the peopling of the Cape' for Camissa Africans, presenting histories 'buried and hidden for centuries', including indigenous figures (Krotoa, Autshumao) and enslaved peoples. Castle official article: local visitors 'focus more on personal or ancestral connections'. Weekend Argus, 17 Apr 2025: National Griqua Council handover ceremony at the Castle, with a Khoi and San council chair describing the Castle as symbolising commitment to preserving Khoi and San traditions and identities.

items.bewering: Dit help hulle om te sien wie hulle is: hul identiteit. So kan die betekenis van 'n historiese plek verander.
items.bron: Castle official article: the ongoing interpretation of the Castle 'reflects broader struggles over memory, identity and justice'; Weekend Argus 2025 (Khoi and San identities at the Castle); gov.za 2016 speech on history helping to 'forge a common identity'.

items.bewering: VOC: Die Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie, 'n Nederlandse handelsmaatskappy wat die Kaap beheer het.
items.bron: Same as the first item: sahistory.org.za 'Dutch settlement'; Stellenbosch ESAT entry on the VOC; Dutch Cape Colony under VOC rule 1652-1795.

items.bewering: handelsmaatskappy: 'n Besigheid wat geld maak deur goedere te koop en te verkoop.
items.bron: Standard meaning of a trading company (a business buying and selling goods for profit); the VOC traded spices, textiles and other goods between Asia and Europe (Stellenbosch ESAT, VOC entry). Accurate as a simplification and consistent with the VOC claim in the study text.

items.bewering: vesting: 'n Sterk gebou met dik mure wat mense teen aanvalle beskerm.
items.bron: Standard meaning of 'vesting' (fortress: a fortified building built to defend against attack); the Castle is described as a bastion fort with thick stone walls (Wikipedia; Castle official site).

items.bewering: koloniale mag: Beheer wat mense van buite oor 'n plek en sy mense neem.
items.bron: Britannica, 'colonialism': control by one power over a dependent area or people, typically by settlers or rulers from outside. The Grade 5 wording keeps the two essentials (control, from outside) and states nothing false.

items.bewering: slaaf: Iemand wat as iemand anders se eiendom gehou is en sonder loon moes werk.
items.bron: Britannica, 'slavery': a condition in which one human being is owned by another and forced to work without pay. Matches.

items.bewering: erfenisterrein: 'n Plek wat bewaar word omdat dit deel van mense se erfenis is.
items.bron: National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999 (SAHRA): heritage sites are places of cultural significance protected for present and future generations. Accurate simplification; the Castle's own status (provincial heritage site) fits it.

items.bewering: museum: 'n Plek waar voorwerpe en stories uit die verlede bewaar en gewys word.
items.bron: ICOM museum definition (2022): an institution that researches, collects, conserves, interprets and exhibits tangible and intangible heritage. Accurate for the history museums this lesson is about.

items.bewering: nasate: Mense wat later in 'n familie gebore word: kinders, kleinkinders en verder.
items.bron: Standard Afrikaans meaning of 'nasaat' (afstammeling: someone descended from a person or group). The examples after the colon (children, grandchildren and on) carry the line of descent. Note for the writer, not a fault: read without its examples, 'later in 'n familie gebore' would also fit a younger brother or sister, who is not a nasaat; the examples prevent that reading as written.

items.bewering: identiteit: Wie 'n mens of 'n groep is, en waar hulle hoort en vandaan kom.
items.bron: Standard meaning of identity as a person's or group's sense of who they are and where they belong; the Castle's identity debates (Castle official article; gov.za 2016 speech) use it in this sense.

opsomming: Elke nagaanbare bewering is bevestig: die VOC en sy beheer van die Kaap, 1666-1679, die dik klipmure, slawe, matrose en soldate as bouers, die Kasteel as erfenisterrein met museums, en dat die museums nou ook slawe- en Khoi- en San-stories vertel. Die les bevat geen superlatiewe en geen vergelykings nie. Die begrip 'nasate' is net reg omdat sy voorbeelde die afstamming dra, dus moet niemand dit inkort nie.
